description: issue #681 (slice I2): a read no host can answer. `spec/interaction-events.md:110-111` gives a blocking read exactly two endings — it runs "until the read finishes or the program is cancelled" — so a headless run with no scripted answer (`executeOptions.hostInput.responses` omitted) takes the second: `ol-limit` with `limit: "cancelled"`, the same identity an externally cancelled run raises, pointed at the waiting `input` call. The program stops there, so the following `print` never runs and no `primitive` event is emitted. Reporting an invented answer (an empty word, say) instead would let the program run on as though the learner had answered — a silent wrong result, which is exactly what a diagnostic exists to prevent.

diagnostics.message: input is waiting for an answer, but this run has no way to supply one, so the program was cancelled before it finished.
